title: Great Flood of Navan
description:
In November 1954, **Navan** experienced catastrophic flooding when the River Boyne burst its banks following days of heavy rainfall across the Boyne catchment area.

The flood was one of the worst natural disasters in the town's modern history. Waters rose rapidly, inundating the town center, damaging hundreds of homes and businesses, and forcing mass evacuations. The bridge crossing the Boyne was severely threatened, and railway lines were submerged, cutting off transport links.

The disaster prompted significant investment in flood defenses and river management along the Boyne. The 1954 flood remains in living memory for many residents and led to improved emergency response planning. Despite subsequent flood defense works, Navan has continued to face periodic flooding, highlighting the ongoing challenge of managing water levels at the confluence of two major rivers.
